Alright, so many of you like to use survey sites. It's not exactly the dream of passive income that we all love, but it's something that usually pays pretty well by beermoney standards depending on the site. The problem is completing surveys. Most sites have you fill out a profile and you're sent surveys that pertain to your demographics, or at least that's the ideal. What ends up happening is:

1) You click on the survey.

2) Enter age.

3) Get disqualified from survey.

Sound familiar? Anyway, I'm no expert on how survey sites operate down to the fine details, but I can tell you what I've gathered based on experience. The trick is to go for what many sites call daily surveys. Daily surveys consistently connect you to survey routers like CINT, Global Test Market, Your Surveys, and so on. The way I'm guessing it works is the survey site you're on connects you to a router, you fill out whatever survey they give you, and they credit your account with $0.75-1.25 depending on which router you're on. The great thing about daily surveys is you will be paid a certain amount per router no matter what the length of the survey is. I've had situations where I took a 3 minute survey (it was on politics) and got $1.00. I'm at the point where I ignore survey invites because of this. Moving on to proper use...

Go for unlimited clicks per day survey routers. Typically, these survey routers pay less per survey, but you are more likely to qualify and they're shorter, so you benefit in the long run. Doing two 10 minute $0.80 surveys is better than one 30 minute $1.00 survey. In addition, these can be completed one after the other an unlimited amount per day. Really easy way to rack up dollars. What gave me the inspiration to write this is that I took the same exact survey 2 times in a row on the same survey router. Got a total of $1.60 in 15 minutes.

Quality Score. Another advantage to using daily survey routers is that they can keep track of quality score. Quality score is determined by completing surveys (kind of like gaining reputation) and by answering those weird quality questions correctly. For instance, when asked how often you bathe in ketchup, say never. With a higher quality score, you're more likely to qualify for surveys. I hardly got rejected after my 8th survey on the same router.

Be honest. Yes, you'll often get matched with surveys that don't really apply to you. I know who you are. You're a boring, average white guy with classes and maybe a day job and you just want some extra money in your PayPal. The stuff I really enjoy is my occasional email from PlayTest Cloud that says, "Spend 15 minutes reviewing this mobile game and get $9!" Y'all gamers should check that out by the way. Anyway, although it may seem appealing to lie in surveys, tell the truth. Even if you are boring, many surveys are region specific. For example, I am from Texas and often get surveys regarding packaging design featuring the Lone Star or other Texas-related symbols.

That's all the free stuff you can do to increase survey site earnings. I based this off of my experience with Clixsense, which is my favorite site for stuff like this primarily due to reliable payments and an amazing staff. They say that you need to receive a check for your first payment, but I sent them a picture of the address on my driver's licence and got my account confirmed for electronic payment in minutes (I use PayPal). If you decide to use their site, I strongly advise use of the Your Surveys router. I rarely get turned down.
